original_question: Which British physician was the first to study the group of genetic diseases that caused Glycogen storage disease type IV?

final_qi.question: Which British physician was the first to study the group of genetic diseases that caused Glycogen storage disease type IV?
final_qi.long_answer: British physician Sir Archibald Garrod (1857–1936) was the first to investigate and define the concept of ‘inborn errors of metabolism,’ the hereditary metabolic disorders that include the various glycogen storage diseases such as Glycogen storage disease type IV. His pioneering work on alkaptonuria and other inherited metabolic defects laid the foundation for recognizing GSD IV as part of this group.

final_answer.long_answer: Sir Archibald Garrod (1857–1936), a British physician, was the first to investigate and define the class of hereditary metabolic disorders he called “inborn errors of metabolism.” His work showed that enzyme deficiencies inherited in a Mendelian fashion could disrupt carbohydrate metabolism, laying the conceptual groundwork for the glycogen storage diseases—including Glycogen storage disease type IV, which is caused by an inherited deficiency of the glycogen-branching enzyme.
